questions.stem: A 20-year-old patient complains of morbid thirst and hyper diuresis (up to 10 Liters daily). Glucose concentration in blood is normal but it is absent in urine. The patient has been diagnosed with diabetes insipidus. What hormonal drug is the most appropriate for the management of this disorder?
questions.solutionHtml:
Vasopressin

Diabetes insipidus is characterized by morbid thirst and hyper diuresis with no alterations of glucose levels in blood and urine. The cause of this disease is the deficiency of vasopressin (antidiuretic hormone), so the administration of vasopressin is the most appropriate treatment.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.454–457, 601–602.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about ADH is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases aquaporin expression on the apical membrane

options.label: B
options.text: It increases urine concentration and decreases urine flow

options.label: D
options.text: Its secretion occurs when plasma osmolality is low

questions.answerText: Its secretion occurs when plasma osmolality is low
questions.solutionHtml:
Its secretion occurs when plasma osmolality is low

ADH secretion reduces when the plasma osmolality becomes low. ADH causes water reabsorption and dilutes the plasma, thereby causing a reduction in plasma osmolality.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.454–457, 601–602

questions.stem: A 57-year-old woman is undergoing a femoral-popliteal bypass for her peripheral vascular disease. The vascular surgeon wishes to induce a localized arteriolar constriction to help control hemostasis. An increase in the local concentration of which of the following agents will cause systemic vasoconstriction?
questions.solutionHtml:
Angiotensin II

Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor that is formed when renin is released from the kidney in response to a fall in blood pressure or vascular volume.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.454–457, 601–602.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man develops a brain tumor that impinges on the supraoptic nucleus in the hypothalamus. As a result, the secretion of which of the following hormones is affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Antidiuretic hormone (ADH)

ADH secretion reduces when the plasma osmolality becomes low. ADH causes water reabsorption and dilutes the plasma, thereby causing a reduction in plasma osmolality. ADH, also called arginine vasopressin, is secreted from the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland (neurohypophysis) into the general circulation from the endings of supra-optic neurons in the hypothalamus.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page No.454–457, 601–602, 1601
